column1:
When and why do you use the
Pretérito perfecto compuesto?
column2:
A past event connected to the present — the time frame is still open, or the result still matters.
  • Within an unclosed period — hoy he trabajado mucho; esta semana he ido tres veces.
  • Recent past — he llegado hace un momento.
  • Life experience, no date given — ¿has estado en México?; nunca he visto la nieve.
  • Present relevance — he perdido las llaves — and I still don't have them.
Regional split: in Spain this is the default for anything today (hoy he comido tarde). In most of Latin America the simple preterite covers that ground (hoy comí tarde).

column1:
Tricks and tips for the
Pretérito perfecto compuesto
column2:
• Learn the irregular participle list once — it serves this and five other compound tenses.
  • The participle never agrees in compound tenses: ella ha hablado, ellas han comido.
  • Nothing comes between haber and the participle: no lo he visto, never he lo visto.
  • Accents break vowel clusters: leído, oído, traído, caído.
  • Time markers that select it in Spain: hoy, esta mañana, esta semana, ya, todavía no, nunca, alguna vez, últimamente.
